customer_acme: hi team — we're seeing intermittent 502/504 from the rerank endpoint when running a ~400 qps load test. p95 latency jumps to 8-12s and then gateway starts returning 502s. not seeing obvious errors in our app logs, can you help triage?

maya: sorry you're hitting this 😞. can you share a minimal repro (curl + payload) and the timeframe (timezone: utc okay)? also, what's your candidate count and timeout settings?

customer_acme: timeframe: today 14:05-14:20 UTC. candidate count = 100, client timeout = 10s, we do 3 retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms). payload sample: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"query":"order best sofa","candidates":["..."/*100 items*/],"max_candidates":100}'```

devon: thanks. first thought: 3 client retries + 10s timeout could be causing retry storms against the gateway when backend is slow. can you paste the exact error body you get on 502/504?

customer_acme: 502 responses look like: `\{"error":"upstream reset"\}`. 504s show as gateway timeout. we also captured a few server-side traces where the request hangs for ~9s before failing.

maya: @devon @sre_jen fyi — customer sees p95 8-12s then 502/504 under load. candidate=100 looks high. can eng-runtime check worker queue/backpressure and kv cache blowups?

sre_jen: on it. I checked infra metrics for that time window: ingress qps spiked, connection queue depth hit 95% of accept backlog on a subset of nodes, and upstream latency (to backend workers) p95 ~7.6s. There were also a handful of worker restarts due to stuck goroutines around 14:12.

samir: possible root causes: (1) client retry amplification, (2) heavy candidate payload causing per-request CPU for scoring, (3) KV cache thrash if many distinct prefixes. quick mitigations: reduce client-side retries, lower max_candidates to 20-30, increase gateway upstream timeout to 30s temporarily so retries don't cascade.

alia-cs: I relayed mitigations to customer: they will lower candidates to 25 and disable retries for a short run. will report back in ~15m.

customer_acme: update — lowering candidates to 25 removes 502s, p95 settles to ~220ms. disabling retries also cut the spike. thanks.

devon: good signal. next steps for us: 1) add a server-side circuit breaker to reject extremely large candidate requests early (400-level rejection) + clear error msg, 2) add burst queueing with backpressure metrics, 3) telemetry to surface candidate_count per request in dashboards, 4) review default client retry guidance in docs.

maya: can eng-runtime make a small guard to cap candidate_count default to 50 and return explicit error when >200 for hosted API? low effort and reduces surface. (cc @samir)

samir: I can prototype a guard in the gateway this afternoon, feature flagged. also will add a telemetry counter for retry storms by client IP/api-key.

sre_jen: ops follow-up: we should increase accept backlog on gateway nodes and tune keepalive for worker pools; I'll open infra ticket.

customer_acme: thanks all — we'll keep an eye and re-open if anything else pops. very helpful suggestions. :pray:

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T15:40:00Z started: patch/guard-cap-candidate (staging).

maya: follow-ups: update docs with recommended candidate_count and retry/backoff, add an FAQ for rerank payload sizing, and create a short postmortem if the guard goes to prod.

devon: marking thread actionable. summary for ticket: high candidate_count + client retries produced retry amplification causing worker queue saturation -> p95 spikes -> gateway timeouts/502s. mitigations applied: customer reduced candidates & disabled retries, gateway guard + telemetry in staging, infra tunes pending.

customer_acme: appreciated!
